paper.citation: Nie, X. and Wager, S. (2021). Quasi-oracle estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects. Biometrika 108(2), 299-319. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asaa076.
paper.source_locator: Section 6.1 'Baseline methods and simulation setups', arXiv:1712.04912v4 (6 Aug 2020) PDF p.15 (general data-generating law) and PDF p.16 (unnumbered Setup A paragraph, since the setups carry no equation numbers: 'We use the scaled Friedman (1991) function ... e*(Xi) = trim0.1{sin(pi Xi1 Xi2)} and tau*(Xi) = (Xi1 + Xi2)/2').

mechanism.name: Nie–Wager (2021) Setup A: Friedman baseline with a sinusoidal propensity

generation_equations.label: Treatment
generation_equations.expression: e(X) = trim_{0.1}{ sin(pi X1 X2) }, trim_eta(u) = max{eta, min(u, 1-eta)}

generation_equations.label: Outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y = b(X) + A tau(X) + sigma eps, eps ~ Normal(0,1), sigma = 1

assumptions: SUTVA: one version of treatment, no interference
Unconfoundedness: treatment depends on X only through sin(pi X1 X2), which is also part of the baseline; the design is observational by construction
Overlap: e(X) is trimmed to [0.1, 0.9], so positivity holds with margin 0.1
Homoscedastic Gaussian noise; sigma = 1 in this scenario

properties.notes: All five coordinates enter the mechanism. The interaction is sin(pi X1 X2) in both the baseline and the propensity, which is why e(X) and b(X) are correlated; the effect surface itself is additive and linear.

estimand.name: tau(x0) = E[Y(1) - Y(0) | X = x0]
estimand.definition: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points; a simple linear surface in the first two coordinates, embedded in a deliberately difficult nuisance structure.

truth.expression: Conditional average treatment effect at the declared query points; a simple linear surface in the first two coordinates, embedded in a deliberately difficult nuisance structure.
truth.derivation: Closed form: the surface is linear in X1, X2, so tau(x0) = (x1 + x2)/2 exactly; cross-checked by a second typing and by the realised outcome column.

adaptations: Dimension fixed at d = 5, the smallest dimension for which the source's baseline is fully defined (it uses X1..X5); the source varies d in {6, 12} for the reported grid.

The source writes Y = b(X) + (W - 0.5) tau(X) + sigma eps; this package uses Y = b(X) + A tau(X) + sigma eps with A in {0,1}. The CATE is unchanged; the marginal outcome law differs by the constant 0.5 tau(X).
Noise scale is fixed at sigma = 1 (the source also reports sigma in {0.5, 2, 3}); those are scenarios, not implemented here.
trim_eta is implemented as np.clip(., 0.1, 0.9), matching trim_0.1 in the source.
